title: docs(changelog): amend the 18.0.0-next.0 entries of lint, service-automation and spec whose sentences the CRUD-filter-operand stage had made false
body:
Fixes #23261
Clause-②: no

This PR amends release-owned text only. It changes the `18.0.0-next.0` entries of five CHANGELOGs: `packages/lint`, `packages/services/service-automation`, `packages/spec`, `packages/cli` and `packages/formula`. In each entry it replaces the sentences that the CRUD-filter-operand stage (S6, `615c696046`) had already made false when the entry was published. The new text is the corrected changeset text that PR #23252 records under `.changeset/pre/`. The PR has no code, no changeset and no entry of any other version.

Written by the `domain:spec` seat 2 dispatch, session `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`. Round 1 (`da548251c`) amended lint, service-automation and spec. The patch round (`baa9e0be0`) adds cli and formula, after the seat re-scoped the claim's file surface in review comment `6155243339` on the card.

## Route: amend in place

AGENTS.md, *Documentation Guardrails*, the `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` row: "Factual error in a released entry → **amend that entry in a dedicated docs-only PR**, ⛔ never an erratum in a later entry and never a rider on code changes — the reader greps the tombstoned symbol and lands on the old entry, so a correction anywhere else is one it never reaches; what shipped stays recorded in the published tarballs and in git history."

Each false sentence is replaced inside the bullet that published it, with the wording of the corrected changeset. So the `18.0.0-next.0` bullet and the GA `18.0.0` bullet (compiled from the same corrected changeset) say the same thing about S6. This PR adds no dated erratum line. PR #22296 took that shape, and its triage asked for it. This card asks for the corrected changeset's text, and an erratum line would make the two entries differ. The shipped wording is still recorded in four places: the npm tarballs, the GitHub Releases, git history, and the BEFORE column below.

## Which sentences, measured

- **S6 is in `18.0.0-next.0`.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor 615c696046 d889448b9` exits 0. `d889448b9` is the Version Packages merge that cut `18.0.0-next.0`. At the cut, `packages/lint/src` has no `flow-filter-token-unknown` rule: the only hits are two comments that call it retired. At `615c696046^` the rule's files exist (`validate-flow-filter-tokens.ts` and its test).
- **S7 (PR #23252, `7958bdf36d`) is not in it.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor 7958bdf36d d889448b9` exits 1. The control leg, `615c696046` on the same checkout and target, exits 0. Read from the content too: at the cut, `service-automation`'s `builtin/template.ts` still exports the single-brace resolver (`interpolate`, `interpolateString`). At this base it exports none of them.
- **The entries are what shipped.** `npm pack` of `@objectstack/lint`, `service-automation`, `spec`, `cli` and `formula` at `18.0.0-next.0` gives a `package/CHANGELOG.md` byte-identical to this PR's base `cc14657ed` (`cmp` exit 0, all five). `next` is `18.0.0-next.0`, the only `next` published.
- **The 15 corrected changesets did not change between the cut and PR #23252.** `git diff --quiet d889448b9 7958bdf36d^` over the 15 files exits 0. So the cut compiled exactly the BEFORE text of PR #23252's table.

PR #23252 corrected each of its 15 files for one of three reasons. This PR takes only the first:

1. **A sentence S6 made false.** False when `18.0.0-next.0` was published. **Amended here.**
2. **A sentence S7 made false.** True of `18.0.0-next.0`, whose code still had the resolver, so it stays: row 11's lint-hint sentence (`:44`) and row 13 (`22301`, which compiles only into `packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md`).
3. **An addition that corrects nothing false.** Row 4's FROM → TO for the retired rule's id and exports (`19939-flow-crud-filter-operands.md:27`). The next.0 bullet says the rule and its exports "are removed", which is true. The added migration map completes the bullet but corrects no false sentence, so it is not in this card's surface. It stays.

## What changed

The tool: each bullet is located by its **full** compiled BEFORE text. That is the changeset at the cut, with the commit hash prefixed and every later line indented two spaces, as `@changesets/cli/changelog` writes it. Each of the 34 bullets matched exactly once, in each CHANGELOG its changeset's frontmatter names, and in no other CHANGELOG. Then only the selected hunks of PR #23252's diff were applied. After the edit, 27 bullets are byte-identical to the compiled corrected changeset. The other 7 (`615c696` in three CHANGELOGs, `6a06e3b` in four) are identical to it except for the hunks left out above (reasons 2 and 3).

Line numbers are at base `cc14657ed`. Version: `18.0.0-next.0` in every row. "Row" is PR #23252's table row.

The cli and formula cells are the patch round. These two changesets also name `@objectstack/cli` (row 11) and `@objectstack/formula` (row 12) in their frontmatter, so their bullets compiled into those CHANGELOGs too. In cli the same `6a06e3b` lint-hint sentence (`:489`, reason 2) stays.

Size: 5 files, +50 / −48 (lint +23 / −21, service-automation +11 / −11, spec +13 / −13, cli +2 / −2, formula +1 / −1). One commit per CHANGELOG.

**Re-check of triage's counts** (`6147677135`), on this PR's head:

- `git grep -c "flow-filter-token-unknown"` gives lint 6, service-automation 3, spec 3. At filing it was 8, 3 and 3. Lint loses the four live-id mentions of rows 2 and 3 and gains the two retirement sentences those rows add. Every remaining hit says the rule retires, or sits in the 17.4.0 entry that introduced it (`:5664` at base), which was true when it shipped.
- `git grep -c "keeps resolving where"`, `"keeps the single-brace dialect"`, `"keeps the template dialect"` and `"a single-brace token in a value position"` give 0 in all five files. The control `git grep -c "## 18.0.0-next.0"` gives 1 in each.
- One `filter: { id: '{uid}' }` stays in each of lint, service-automation and spec, in `615c696`'s "Who is affected" line. It describes a remedy text that S6 itself migrated, so it is history.

**Nothing outside the `18.0.0-next.0` sections moved.** In each of the five files, the text from the `## 17.7.0` heading to the end of the file has the same sha256 at base and at head. The header lines are unchanged. Every hunk ends before the `## 17.7.0` heading.

## Not changed, on purpose

- Row 11's `:44` lint-hint sentence ("…and every other position keeps the single brace."), lint `:1018`, service-automation `:347`, spec `:384`, cli `:489`: true of `18.0.0-next.0`. S7 changed that hint.
- Row 4's `:27` FROM → TO addition: completes the bullet, corrects no false sentence (see above).
- Row 13 (`22301`): S7, and it compiles only into `packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md`, outside this card.
- Every other version's entry, including lint 17.4.0's `flow-filter-token-unknown` introduction.

## No ripple

Several tools read these files mechanically: `check-release-notes`, `check-release-page-status`, `check-release-section-coverage`, `sync-release-index-currency`, `check-docs-image-tag`, `check-future-spec-major` and `release-github-releases`. They all read version headings or a whole section. None pins a bullet line. No version heading or bullet hash changes here. No docs page is generated from these files.

## Changeset: none, labelled `skip-changeset`

`CHANGELOG.md` is in the `files[]` of all five packages, so the next tarball of each ships the amended entry. `changeset version` prepends new entries and keeps this one. A changeset would compile the correction into a new entry under a later version, which is the "erratum in a later entry" the guardrail rules out. It follows PR #22296.

## Verification (head `baa9e0be0`)

- **Derived gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with no paths, on `baa9e0be0`, derives **59** commands. They are byte-identical to round 1's list on `da548251c`. First, `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/lint...' build` ran under the verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, held 3m04s), which left the working tree clean. Each command then ran once, with its exit code captured before any pipe.
  - **57 exit 0.** Among them: `check:nul-bytes` (11284 text files, no raw ASCII control bytes), `check:release-notes`, `check:release-page-status`, `check-release-section-coverage` (plain, `--strict` and `--self-test`), `check:published-files`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:doc-authoring`, `docs-audit/check-affected-docs`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` and `check:docs-transcript-drift` ("4 declared transcript value(s) across 414 page(s) under content/docs/ equal what the registry derives today").
  - **Two of those 57 swept only the 4 built packages** of the lint closure: `check:dts-closure` ("4 built package(s) swept - 46/46 declared declaration file(s) present") and `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` ("4 built package(s) swept - 58 map(s), none embed source text"). Each is exit 0 over that population, not the workspace. This partial sweep is declared, as is the narrowing below.
  - **2 NOT MEASURED**, each exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET): `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure`. Both need a full workspace build. This narrowing is declared: the diff changes no source byte, and a build compiles `src/` and never reads `CHANGELOG.md`. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs them after its own build.
  - `--ran` reports: "✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 59 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 57 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)."
- **Tests and typecheck: none owed.** No TypeScript is touched. No test reads these CHANGELOG lines: the tests that walk the tree skip `CHANGELOG.md` by name, and no test or gate pins a bullet of these entries.

- **ESLint, a measured narrowing:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 5 changed files reports 5 files, each with 0 errors and the single warning "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied". `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so the diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.
- **Control bytes:** `grep -naP` for raw control bytes over the 5 files matches nothing (exit 1; a control file with one control byte answers exit 0).

## Acceptance notes

- **The GitHub Releases still carry the old text.** The bodies of `@objectstack/lint`, `service-automation`, `spec`, `cli` and `formula` at `18.0.0-next.0` were compiled from these sections when the version was published. Each still carries S6-false sentences: service-automation and spec have 7 "keeps resolving where" lines each and cli has 1; lint and formula have the "keeps the single-brace dialect" line. Lint's body is cut at the API limit before its later bullets. Editing a Release is the maintainer's act, so it is not done here. Like the tarballs, those bodies record what shipped.
- **The same claim, in spec source (filed by the seat as #23338, not edited: code).** Two ADR-0087 D3 entries still prescribe "Rename every read of the old name with it — a text-slot hole, a CEL expression, a single-brace token in a value position": `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-binding-name-dollar-refused.ts:35` and `18.flow-binding-variable-dollar-name-refused.ts:28`, both in `replacement`. Their changesets (rows 14 and 15) were corrected. The published `@objectstack/spec@18.0.0-next.0` ships this text in `dist/migrations/index.js`, `dist/migrations/index.mjs` and `spec-changes.json` (grep of the unpacked tarball).
- **Noted, not filed:** the header of `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.text-slot.test.ts:23` says "Every other notify / screen string keeps the single-brace dialect". A test comment, not shipped. Carrier: the next PR that edits that file.
